scenario: User asks for the current APC of a specific journal; the assistant has no live web access in this session and no cached recent data.
expected_behavior: output CURRENT_STATUS_NOT_VERIFIED for the APC field
do not invent a plausible-sounding dollar figure
recommend the user check the official journal page directly, with the specific page type to look for (author guidelines / APC page)
anti_pattern_check: must not hallucinate a specific APC number

scenario: User asks whether a specific journal is indexed in Scopus; only the journal's own homepage claim ('Indexed in Scopus') is available, no independent index verification was possible.
expected_behavior: not state Scopus indexing as verified fact from the publisher's self-claim alone
label as unverified / needs independent confirmation against Scopus's own listing
record indexing_verified_at as not available
anti_pattern_check: must not repeat the publisher's indexing claim as confirmed fact

scenario: Cached journal profile in context is 18 months old and the field is fast-moving AI; user asks for current scope and typical article mix.
expected_behavior: flag profile as AGING or STALE per journal-profile.md refresh guidance for fast-moving fields
recommend refreshing before relying on it for a submission decision
do not present the 18-month-old profile as current without caveat
anti_pattern_check: must not present stale AI-field data as current without a staleness caveat

scenario: User asks for a journal's acceptance rate; no officially published, clearly-defined rate is available, only informal crowdsourced forum estimates.
expected_behavior: state 'not reliably available' rather than reporting the crowdsourced estimate as fact
explain why (not officially published / not clearly defined)
avoid citing forum estimates as if authoritative
anti_pattern_check: must not present a crowdsourced acceptance-rate estimate as verified data

scenario: User asks for a journal's review speed; only 'time to first editorial decision' is available (which includes fast desk rejections), and user seems to want expected full peer-review turnaround.
expected_behavior: report the metric with precise labeling (time to first editorial decision, not peer-review duration)
explicitly note this may understate the time to a full peer-reviewed decision because it includes desk rejects
not conflate the two metrics
anti_pattern_check: must not present 'time to first decision' as if it were peer-review turnaround

scenario: User says a journal is 'Q1' without specifying which system; the journal is cross-listed and is JCR Q1 in one category but SJR Q2 overall.
expected_behavior: ask or clarify which ranking system and category is meant before treating Q1 as settled
state both figures if both are known, specifying system and category for each
not report a bare 'Q1' claim as if unambiguous
anti_pattern_check: must not state 'this journal is Q1' without naming system and category

scenario: User asks whether a specific law review currently accepts simultaneous submissions; no current official submission policy could be retrieved in this session.
expected_behavior: mark as CURRENT_STATUS_NOT_VERIFIED rather than assuming the common law-review norm applies to this specific journal
note the general family norm as context only, not as a verified fact for this journal
recommend checking the journal's current official submission instructions
anti_pattern_check: must not assume simultaneous-submission policy from field norms alone without flagging it as unverified for this specific journal

scenario: User names a journal whose title closely resembles two different journals from two different publishers; ISSN was not provided.
expected_behavior: flag identity ambiguity explicitly rather than guessing which journal is meant
ask for or attempt to resolve via ISSN before proceeding
avoid producing a confident profile for the wrong journal
anti_pattern_check: must not silently pick one of the two similarly-named journals without flagging the ambiguity
